summary: First iteration testing of greyhound lay-betting simulator. Backend: 9/9 pytest tests passed covering session CRUD, race generation (6 unique traps, ranks by ascending odds), lay bet placement, recovery chain math (L0->L3 transitions, bust on 4th loss, reset on win), stop conditions (manual, max_races, 400 on inactive next-race), and 404s. Frontend: New Session dialog opens, accepts inputs, creates session, dashboard shows config + stats, Run Next Race advances races, race card renders runners/odds/lay bets/winner, recovery panel updates, race history grows.

ui_bugs.issue: After clicking stop-session-btn, the visible badge still read 'Active' in the test run. Backend stop endpoint works correctly (status=stopped_manual confirmed via pytest). Possible UI state-sync issue OR test artifact (multiple active sessions in archive). Worth verifying that the currently-loaded session UI updates immediately after Stop click.

action_items: Verify Stop button updates session-status-badge immediately on the active session view (backend works; check frontend state sync after POST /sessions/{id}/stop).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py uses deprecated FastAPI @app.on_event('shutdown') - migrate to lifespan handlers.
RecoveryChain bust path sets pending_stake=INITIAL_STAKE (commented 'not used') - acceptable but ensure UI hides pending_stake for busted chains.
No upper bound enforced on bank/total_pnl rounding edge cases at very long sessions, but within MAX_RECOVERY_LEVEL=3 it stays bounded.
Pydantic Session model not stripping mongo _id explicitly via model - currently relies on projection {'_id':0}; safe but consider centralizing.
seed_data_creation: Tests create and delete their own sessions via fixtures; no persistent seed data left behind.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest at /app/backend/tests/test_simulator.py covers all CRUD, race gen invariants, recovery math (40-race randomized chain validation), stop conditions, 404s. Re-run with: REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<url> pytest /app/backend/tests/test_simulator.py -v. Frontend critical flow validated end-to-end. Only remaining check is the Stop button -> badge UI sync.
rca of the issue: Stop badge UI: backend stop endpoint returns status='stopped_manual' correctly (verified by test_stop_session). If badge still shows 'Active' in UI, root cause is likely that the frontend stop handler is not refetching or replacing the active-session state after the response - check /app/frontend/src/App.js stopSession handler to ensure it updates the activeSession state with the response payload.
